evidence.quote: “Patient” means that we see no need to rush to judgment. It may be some time before the outlook for jobs and inflation calls clearly for a change in policy.
Today we announced that we intend to slow the runoff of our assets starting in May and to cease runoff entirely in September of this year.
And I don’t feel that we have kind of convincingly achieved our 2 percent mandate in a symmetrical way.
Data arriving since September suggest that growth is slowing somewhat more than expected.
And just as strong global growth was a tailwind, weaker global growth can be a headwind to our economy.
we don’t see any data pushing us to move rates in either direction, and we’re going to watch carefully and patiently as we allow events to evolve.

parsed.rationale: The Chair holds rates, adopts a patient wait-and-see stance, ends balance sheet runoff early, and emphasizes muted inflation and downside global/growth risks, a dovish shift from prior tightening. Guidance is symmetric in wording ('either direction') so the lean is moderate rather than an explicit easing signal.
